title: A random forest ranks mortality-associated markers in the Italian CORIST cohort
summary: An exploratory random forest analysis of 3,894 hospitalized COVID-19 patients ranked renal function, C-reactive protein and age as influential mortality-classification features. Conventional survival analyses in the same cohort supported associated risks. These retrospective findings are neither causal effects nor an independently validated clinical risk tool.
ai_technology: Random forest, permutation feature importance and k-nearest-neighbor imputation
organization: Mediterranea Cardiocentro; IRCCS Neuromed; CORIST collaboration

evidence.tested: The retrospective 30-center Italian cohort included 3,894 patients admitted from February 19 to May 23, 2020; 712 died and 532 were still hospitalized at the May 29 cutoff. RF development used 2,725 patients and a random 1,169-patient test subset, with training hyperparameter search. Renal function and C-reactive protein ranked above age in the reported feature-importance analysis; conventional Cox models analyzed associations with time to in-hospital death.
evidence.unknown: Imputation and normalization are described before the train/test split, without clear fold-specific fitting. Although Methods discuss test-set importance, the primary figure caption places the permutation-importance analysis in the training sample; this record does not claim independently reproduced feature rankings. The test subset came from the same pooled cohort, not a new hospital or external population. Ongoing hospitalization at cutoff complicates a binary death/no-death target. High reported survival sensitivity coexisted with low specificity; overall accuracy is not validated mortality sensitivity. Missing smoking/obesity data, absent vital signs, treatment differences and residual confounding limit interpretation. Cox hazard ratios are conventional same-cohort associations, not AI-derived causal findings.
evidence.ai_role: The learned forest and permutation analysis provided an exploratory nonlinear feature ranking; conventional survival modeling supplied complementary association estimates. Their agreement is not independent confirmation.

source_review.scope: Original primary computational Methods, cohort/reference definitions, represented Results and bounded limitations actually read; no code executed or independent reanalysis.
